evidence.claim: Colorado DOT gives a driving time of 90 minutes and emphasizes the contrast between high peaks, riverside stretches, working ranches and natural hot springs.
evidence.quote: The constantly unfolding views of impressive peaks, intermittent stretches of lush riverside, numerous fishing and boater access points, extensive national forest and other public lands, active high altitude ranches and an variety of commercially developed natural hot springs together define the amazing scenic, recreational and geological contrasts

evidence.claim: It is a Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway, following the upper Arkansas past eight of the Rocky Mountains’ highest peaks.
evidence.quote: The Collegiate Peaks Scenic Byway is a 57-mile (92 km) Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway located in Chaffee and Lake counties, Colorado, US. The Byway follows the upper Arkansas River past the Collegiate Peaks, featuring eight of the highest peaks in the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.claim: Side trips reach the mining towns of Vicksburg, Winfield and St. Elmo; aquamarine, Colorado’s state gemstone, is mined on Mount Antero.
evidence.quote: Nowhere else in Colorado is found the state gemstone, the aquamarine, mined on Mt. Antero. The classic mining towns of Vicksburg, Winfield and St. Elmo are accessible from the byway

evidence.claim: By 1877, the Leadville Stagecoach Road ran through Granite, carrying supplies and mail as well as passengers.
evidence.quote: by 1877 the Leadville Stagecoach Road was running from Canyon City, through Granite, Leadville, and north to Denver.  Reliable transportation was important to deliver supplies for the growing communities, and the route was used more as a supply and mail route than for transportation of passengers.

evidence.claim: Traces of that earlier road remain, while Highway 24 runs on the river’s west side.

evidence.claim: The stage road through Granite survives as a hiking and cycling trail.

evidence.claim: Start at Granite on the Arkansas, between the Mosquito and Sawatch ranges, and head south toward Buena Vista.
evidence.quote: Situated between the Mosquito and the Sawatch mountain ranges, Granite is a high mountain town located on the Arkansas River midway between Leadville to the north, and Buena Vista to the south.

evidence.claim: At Nathrop, Chalk Creek meets the Arkansas beneath the valley of Mount Princeton and Mount Antero.
evidence.quote: Mount Antero borders the southern side of the river, while Mount Princeton borders the northern side.

evidence.claim: At Nathrop, Chalk Creek meets the Arkansas
evidence.quote: The river empties into the Arkansas River at the town of Nathrop, Colorado.

evidence.claim: Continue to Salida, named for the river’s exit from the valley into Bighorn Sheep Canyon.
evidence.quote: Salida, meaning "exit" in Spanish, was named on account of its location near the point where the Arkansas River flows out of the valley and into Bighorn Sheep Canyon

evidence.claim: Heaps of rounded granite boulders along the Arkansas mark the work of placer miners.
evidence.quote: Signs of placer mining  up and down along the Arkansas river near Granite and the surrounding areas are in evidence  by the many heaps of glacially rounded granite boulders

evidence.claim: They used sluice boxes to separate heavy gold flakes from gravel washed along by the current.
evidence.quote: The gravel was carried  down the entire length of the sluice and then discharged, but the heavier flakes of gold settled and became trapped.

evidence.claim: After gold was found in Low Pass Gulch in 1867, Granite drew miners from nearby Cache Creek.
evidence.quote: Following the discovery of gold in Low Pass Gulch in 1867, the town of Granite, located on either side of the Arkansas river, attracted many of the miners who previously inhabited the town of Cache Creek.

evidence.claim: Prospecting later moved into the hills in search of gold-bearing veins; old hard-rock mining tunnels remain there.

evidence.claim: As the ore diminished, the town’s population declined.
evidence.quote: In just a few years their ore began to play out, and the town's population, once as high as 7000, began to decline.
